body.working_title: What error measures reward: simulations of RMSE, MAE, MAPE and sMAPE

body.text: Brief requirements (the supervisor, 2026-11-14): (1) a study separate from the review entrylib:2026.000008, supporting its claims; (2) simulations with simple models; (3) the measures MAE, RMSE, MAPE and sMAPE; (4) what each measure recommends: the point forecast or method it selects; (5) a variety of situations; (6) a plan and hypotheses, recorded with claimset lab. The script lines that meet each are listed once the script exists.

Which point forecasts and which forecasting methods do RMSE, MAE, MAPE and sMAPE select when outcomes are symmetric, skewed or intermittent, and when series differ in scale, and do their choices agree with the claims of the review entrylib:2026.000008@v2?

body.text: The supervisor's changes to the design, 2026-11-14, before any run: intermittent outcomes are defined by more than 50% zeros; sMAPE scores a pair with y = f as 0; the sMAPE hypothesis is about the mean (H13), with a second about the median (H14); a hypothesis that sMAPE selects zero on intermittent outcomes (H15, the supervisor's expectation); Poisson outcomes are added; every decision rule uses 99% confidence intervals (1% level), not p-values; SES on logs is kept. The MAPE hypothesis stays about the median (H16): on lognormal outcomes the median lies below the mean, so a forecast below the median is below the mean too, the stronger test of the claim that MAPE suits neither.

body.design: The oracle design: for each of 17 settings (normal; lognormal s = 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1; Poisson lambda = 1.5, 3.5, 10; intermittent negative binomial mean = 0.3, 0.5, 0.6 and Poisson lambda = 0.3, 0.5, 0.65), 200 replications (seeds 1 to 200 with the setting's index) of 100,000 draws. Each candidate on a grid (continuous outcomes: 0.2 to 3.0 times the median in steps of 0.005; counts: 0 to max(3 mean, mean + 6 sqrt(mean) + 2) in steps of 0.01) is scored by RMSE, MAE, MAPE (continuous outcomes only) and sMAPE (a pair with y = f scores 0); each measure's selected forecast is the lowest-scoring candidate. code/oracle.py --seed 1 --reps 200 --n 100000.
body.analysis: Per setting and measure, the mean selected forecast over the 200 replications with its 99% confidence interval (mean +/- 2.576 sd / sqrt(200)). A setting's interval reaches a target (the mean, the median, or zero) if it does once widened by half a grid step on each side, which the grid cannot resolve; it lies below (above) the target otherwise. Per hypothesis, the script counts the settings it covers and how many reach, lie below and lie above the target. For RMSE and MAE selecting the same on normal outcomes: the 99% interval of the per-replication difference (MAE minus RMSE selection), widened by one grid step, reaches 0 or not. On counts, a selection of 0 is the grid's natural floor, not an edge problem.

body.definition: Outcomes from a symmetric distribution with heavier tails than the normal, mean and median 100 and standard deviation 10: Laplace with scale 10 / sqrt(2), and 100 + (10 / sqrt(3)) t with t from a Student t distribution with 3 degrees of freedom, whose tails are heavier than Laplace's and whose fourth moment is infinite, so large outliers are frequent.

Outcomes y = 100 exp(x), x from a Laplace distribution with location 0 and scale b, b in {0.25, 0.5}: positive and right-skewed with heavier tails than lognormal outcomes; median 100, mean 100 / (1 - b^2). Heavier tails on the log scale would leave y with no finite mean.

Series with log y_t = l_t + e_t, l_t = l_{t-1} + u_t, u_t ~ N(0, (0.3 s)^2), l_0 = log(100), s in {0.25, 0.5}, and noise e_t of standard deviation s from one of three families: normal; Laplace (scale s / sqrt(2)); or outliers, a contaminated normal in which 95% of e_t are N(0, c^2) and 5% are N(0, (4c)^2), c = s / sqrt(1.75). An in-sample part of n = 10, 30, 50, 100, 500 or 1,000 observations is followed by 12 held out and forecast. All three families are symmetric, so exp(l_t) is the median of y_t; noise heavier-tailed than Laplace on the log scale would leave y with no finite mean.

body.design: The oracle design: 18 settings (normal; Laplace and Student t with 3 degrees of freedom, both symmetric with mean 100 and standard deviation 10; lognormal s = 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1; log-Laplace b = 0.25, 0.5; Poisson lambda = 1.5, 3.5, 10; intermittent negative binomial mean = 0.3, 0.5, 0.6 and Poisson lambda = 0.3, 0.5, 0.65) x test-set sizes n = 10, 30, 50, 100, 500, 1,000 and 100,000; 1,000 replications per setting and size under 100,000 and 200 at 100,000 (seeds 1, 2, ... with the setting's index and n). Each candidate on a grid (continuous outcomes: 0.2 to 3.0 times the median in steps of 0.005; counts: 0 to max(3 mean, mean + 6 sqrt(mean) + 2) in steps of 0.01; extended by its own step, up to 20 times, whenever a selection lands on its upper edge or on a lower edge above zero) is scored by RMSE, MAE, MAPE (continuous outcomes only) and sMAPE (a pair with y = f scores 0); each measure's selected forecast is the lowest-scoring candidate. claimset-code/prediction-simulations/oracle.py --seed 1 --sizes 10 30 50 100 500 1000 100000 --reps-small 1000 --reps-large 200 (numpy 2.5.3).
body.analysis: Per setting, size and measure: the mean selected forecast over replications and its standard error. A hypothesis covering k intervals (its settings x the 7 sizes) uses intervals mean +/- z se with z for two-sided 1 - 0.01/k (Bonferroni), each widened by half a grid step, which the grid cannot resolve; an interval reaches the target (the mean, the median or zero) or lies wholly below or above it. The script counts, per hypothesis, the intervals and how many reach, lie below and lie above. For RMSE and MAE on normal outcomes: the per-replication difference (MAE minus RMSE selection), with its interval widened by one grid step, reaches 0 at each size or not; this covers the 3 symmetric settings (normal, Laplace, Student t) x 7 sizes = 21 intervals. On counts, a selection of 0 is the grid's natural floor, not an edge problem.

body.design: 2,000 multiplicative local level series per noise family (normal; Laplace; outliers: 5% of observations four times as spread), noise level (s = 0.25, 0.5, the standard deviation of the log-scale noise in every family) and in-sample size (n = 10, 30, 50, 100, 500, 1,000), each followed by 12 held-out values (seeds 1 with the family's, the level's index and n). ETS(A,N,N) is fitted to the logs of the in-sample part by statsforecast's AutoETS(model='ANN') (statsforecast 2.1.1); its median forecast exp(m_h) and mean forecast exp(m_h + v_h / 2) are scored on the held-out values. Under Laplace and outlier noise the mean forecast keeps the normal correction exp(v_h / 2), as an analyst using the model would: it is the model's mean forecast, not the exact mean. claimset-code/prediction-simulations/models.py --seed 1 --series 2000 --sizes 10 30 50 100 500 1000 --noises normal Laplace outliers.
body.analysis: Per series: the MSE of the mean forecast minus that of the median forecast, divided by exp(2 m_1); and the MAE of the median forecast minus that of the mean forecast, divided by exp(m_1). Per noise family, level and size, the mean over series and its standard error. Each hypothesis covers 36 intervals (3 families x 2 levels x 6 sizes), each at two-sided 1 - 0.01/36 (Bonferroni); a negative interval favours the forecast the hypothesis names. The script counts the intervals wholly below zero, wholly above zero and reaching zero.
